reaction.episode: Active DIGESTION episode, data through October 23 (not stale): SPX 7623.68 is 2.82% below its 120-day high, 0.99% below its 50-day and 4.56% above its 200-day; SMH 527.20 sits BETWEEN_ZONES (Zone 1: 540-565, Zone 2: 470-505) and NVDA 210.96 sits above Zone 1 (200-210, Zone 2: 175-185); VIX is 19.45 at its 5-day high, HY OAS is calm at 3.23, and the mechanical capitulation tally is only 1 of 4 (credit calm alone).
reaction.invalidation: A held SPX close above the 7750-7820 failure zone with SMH reclaiming its 50-day proves Watch too cautious (the episode is over and positioning should have started); conversely, HY OAS above 4% or an SPX close below its 200-day proves Watch too complacent (the digestion is a regime break, not a pullback). Either print voids this ladder.

ladder.response: Prepare Tranche A sizing against those prints, but do not execute on the print alone — require the mechanical tally to rise from 1/4 (zone occupancy plus at least one of volume climax reversal or VIX rollover) before any Probe.
ladder.trigger: SMH prints into Zone 2 (470-505) or NVDA prints into Zone 2 (175-185).

ladder.response: Treat it as the trap case: no chasing the bounce, no entries into strength. The failed retest confirms Watch; only a held close above the zone disarms this rung.
ladder.trigger: A bounce carries SPX into the 7750-7820 failure zone (SMH 580-600) and fails to hold a close above it.

ladder.response: Stand down: the digestion read is broken, the ladder is void, and the book re-audits from scratch. No Probe or Add until a new episode state is computed.
ladder.trigger: HY OAS breaks above 4% (from 3.23) or SPX closes below its 200-day (7291.31).

ladder.response: Episode over: revisit stance toward Probe/Add on the quality dislocations (AVGO, NVDA, BWXT) whose revenues confirm the setup, sized off the reclaimed levels.
ladder.trigger: A held SPX close above 7750-7820 with SMH reclaiming its 50-day (575.09).

ladder.response: Probe only, sized small: the capitulation confirmation earns a first tranche at zone levels, not a full Add — the failure zone above still caps the trade until reclaimed.
ladder.trigger: The mechanical tally rises from 1/4 on zone occupancy plus a volume climax reversal or VIX rollover from 19.45, without yet reclaiming the failure zone.

reaction.trapRisk: The pivot-and-fail scenario is the live risk, not a hypothetical: SPX already closed Friday at 7623.68 back below the 7750-7820 zone after failing there, so the next bounce into that zone is guilty until proven innocent. Entries change accordingly — no chasing the first bounce, no buying strength into the zone, and no treating an intraday poke above 7820 as a reclaim. Only a held close above the zone, or a zone-down print (SMH 470-505 / NVDA 175-185) with tally confirmation, earns an entry; everything between those levels is waiting room.

strategyPosture: Watch through the October 28 FOMC. No zone occupancy (SMH between zones, NVDA above Zone 1), a mechanical capitulation tally of only 1 of 4, SPX below its 50-day and below the 7750-7820 failure zone: this is a tape to let come to the ladder's levels, not to chase. New money stays in bills until a zone print plus tally confirmation, or a held reclaim of the failure zone, says otherwise.

themes.counterRead: Rotation is the right label only while credit stays loose — the divergence itself is real and worth tracking, since credit conditions can flip. If lending standards tighten or HY OAS breaks out, this theme reprices from rotation to rollover, and the index-level calm will stop being a comfort.
themes.dataAnchor: The concentration read is ROTATION_NOT_ROLLOVER: the Mag 7 average sits 13.99% below 52-week highs against SPY's 2.8%, an 11.19-point divergence gap, with TSLA the weakest at 25.4% below its high and only AAPL near its high at 1.1% below. Bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 0%, far below the ~40% stress threshold), so the credit leg of a true rollover is absent. The damage is concentrated in the names that dominate the index, not broad: QQQ is down 4.89% over the month against SPY's 0.79%.
themes.label: Rotation, Not Rollover — Index Calm Masks Leadership Damage
themes.narrative: The headline tape looks contained: SPY sits only 2.8% below its 52-week high and the S&P is down just 0.79% over the last month, which reads as an orderly pullback.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS moving from 3.23 toward 4% or lending standards leaving the LOOSE zone — either flips this theme from rotation to rollover.

themes.counterRead: Dislocation is not a bottom. SMH at 527.20 sits BETWEEN_ZONES — below Zone 1 (540-565) and above Zone 2 (470-505) — NVDA at 210.96 sits above Zone 1 (200-210), and the mechanical capitulation tally is only 1 of 4. Multiple compression can run further without any fundamental break, so these names are research targets for zone prints, not buys on the dislocation alone.
themes.dataAnchor: The fundamentals in the input run the other way. AVGO is 35% below its high while revenue grows 55% YoY with a 42.1% FCF margin (conviction score 84, tier A). LRCX is 47.5% below its high on 131.3% revenue growth; ONTO is 48.6% below on 22.1% growth; CLS is 45.1% below on 57.8% growth; NVDA is only 13.3% below its high on 61.4% revenue growth. Even AMAT, 49% below its high, grows revenue 11.4% — but its decline reason is MULTIPLE_COMPRESSION, not broken fundamentals. RSI readings across the group (24.6-38.2) show washout, not orderly drift.
themes.label: AI Semiconductor Dislocation — Revenues Growing, Multiples Compressing
themes.narrative: The market narrative says the AI trade is broken: the semiconductor complex has sold off 30-50% from highs and SMH is down 21.53% from its 120-day high.
themes.watchFor: SMH printing into Zone 2 (470-505) or NVDA into Zone 2 (175-185) with the mechanical tally rising from 1/4 — that combination, not the dislocation depth, is the entry trigger.

themes.counterRead: Separate the growers from the story names. BWXT's drawdown against growing revenue is the DATA_AHEAD setup; VST's insider buying does not override deteriorating revenue, so it stays a watchlist name with a promotion condition, not a buy on insider flow alone. The theme-wide derating is the opportunity only where revenue confirms it.
themes.dataAnchor: The 1-month tape is indiscriminate: SMR -37.19%, OKLO -31.26%, URA -16.37%, PWR -15.31%, GEV -14.87%, CCJ -10.80%. But the fundamentals split the group. BWXT is 47.4% below its high while revenue grows 26.1% YoY (recovery confirmed, watchlist promotion score 77). VST is 31.2% below its high and insiders bought $1.17M at the trough — yet its revenue inflection is DETERIORATING, the exception in the group.
themes.label: Nuclear / AI-Power Washout — Growers Sold With the Story Names
themes.narrative: The nuclear/AI-power theme has been sold as a single story: the whole complex is down double digits over the last month, which reads as the theme being dead.
themes.watchFor: VST revenue inflection turning from DETERIORATING to recovery, or BWXT holding a zone print — either separates the growers from the story names.

themes.counterRead: Credit calm is a lagging comfort. VIX closed Friday at 19.45 — its 5-day high and up 30.8% over 20 days — while SPX slipped below its 50-day (7623.68 vs 7699.64, -0.99%). Equity stress is rising before credit moves, and the FOMC decision on October 28 is the next repricing event for both. If credit follows equities, the contained read breaks.
themes.dataAnchor: Credit has not cracked: HY OAS is 3.23 and calm, the 2s10s curve is positive at +0.22 (2Y 4.77, 10Y 4.99), the real 10-year is 2.64, and the funds rate is 3.88. That matches the contained index drawdown — SPX only 2.82% below its 120-day high of 7844.52 and still 4.56% above its 200-day. One honesty flag: this run's FRED feed came in PARTIAL, so rate prints are last-good cache where the feed failed, not fresh prints.
themes.label: Credit and Rates Contained — But Equity Stress Is Rising First
themes.narrative: The rates narrative says tight money is driving the drawdown, with the 10-year near 5% and the curve under pressure.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS breaking above 4% or the 10-year repricing sharply around the October 28 FOMC — either voids the contained-credit read.

themes.counterRead: A falling premium is not a buy signal and not a ladder name: BMNR is excluded from the deployment ladder by standing rule, and dislocation alone never promotes a holding. The action here is position-size awareness — these names set the book's downside beta — not adding on weakness.
themes.dataAnchor: The tape says otherwise. Over the last month CONL fell 34.28% (-5.72% on Friday alone), BMNR fell 20.05%, ETH-USD fell 14.64%, and COIN fell 17.53%. Both CONL and BMNR are current holdings, so this is book damage, not watchlist theory. The premium complex is leading the drawdown, not cushioning it.
themes.label: Leveraged and Crypto-Adjacent Beta Leads the Drawdown
themes.narrative: The leveraged and crypto-treasury premium story — that these vehicles deserve a persistent premium to their underlying — is still priced into these names.
themes.watchFor: CONL or BMNR stabilizing relative to ETH itself — premium compression stopping — before any sizing discussion reopens.

A held SPX close above the 7750-7820 failure zone (with SMH reclaiming its 50-day at 575.09) — the reclaim that disarms the trap read.
The mechanical capitulation tally rising from 1/4 via zone occupancy, a volume climax reversal, or a VIX rollover from 19.45.
HY OAS breaking above 4% from 3.23 — the stand-down condition for the whole ladder.
The October 28 FOMC repricing the 10-year (currently 4.99) and the curve (currently +0.22) in either direction.
whereWaveBuilds: The next move materializes at SMH Zone 2 (470-505) or on a retest of the SPX 7750-7820 failure zone. The October 28 FOMC is the trigger that forces one of those two paths — a hawkish surprise pushes the complex toward Zone 2, a dovish one sets up the failure-zone retest that must then prove itself with a held close.
